synopsis: The strategy requires measuring the existing warning system in virtual environments, comparing the new system in the same environments, and using simulation to improve it against that baseline [f25, f26, f27]. The established off-field method is replaying raw sensor logs against independent ground truth; baseline quality depends on recording coverage, and using the production detector's own outputs as truth makes missed objects disappear from the assessment [f94, f271, f5359]. Measurement should be encounter-based and stratified by object class, distance and condition, with warning rates, timing and operational availability reported rather than hidden in fleet averages; glossary sample-size guidance specifies 59 consecutive successful encounters per stratum for a 95% detection claim and 299 for a 99% claim [f14339, f14340, f14342, f14347]. Recording should start in October 2026, with the old-system baseline and supporting validation infrastructure ideally ready by mid-2027, before prototype-dependent work becomes the bottleneck [f5168, f5615, f5616]. A central tension is that matching or beating the warning system is not an adequate braking acceptance target: common stages can be compared, but braking must be assessed in closed loop against new hazard-derived requirements [f27, f111, f5500, f12188].
